_comment: Ordered dispatch queue for everything not yet done. `after` names dispatch slugs (from dispatch.json) or queue ids that must land first. `conflicts` names slugs whose files overlap — do not run both at once. Six concurrent agents is the ceiling: four agents plus the orchestrator hit the session limit twice on 2026-09-06, and the cap is usage, not wall-clock.

units.title: Remote Control privilege policy and lock-state policy, wired end to end
units.note: Both are already implemented on task/p0-013-request-origin and land as `partial`. P0-014's remainder is a real FIDO/WebAuthn path behind --origin-policy remote. P0-015's remainder is that nothing reports lock state: APEX Shell locks with ext-session-lock and never calls SetLockedHint, so logind reports LockedHint=no on a session locked for an hour. The shell half was recovered from a WIP snapshot and pushed as fix/locked-hint at 87c84f3 (LockedHintService.qml, qmldir, Lockscreen.qml wiring) — integrate that first. P0-015 criterion 2 also needs P0-007's session grants to exist. P0-005's agent also produced an apex-shell branch, task/p0-005-agent-center-modes (the row shows the mode an agent is in) — integrate it alongside the apex-os side.

units.title: Cloudflare R2, D1/KV/Queues/Hyperdrive, DNS capability sets
units.note: 26 of section 13.2's 32 operations remain after P1-002 took seven. Two framework gaps the Cloudflare author hit and worked around locally, which P1-005 should fix generally rather than repeat: Bound carries no provider payload, so bind cannot hand what it resolved to perform — Cloudflare re-resolves and refuses on mismatch, but git does NOT, which makes git's host pin a TOCTOU rather than a guarantee; and mint cannot reach a companion service, which is why OAuth refresh could not be expressed as mint and why P1-011 will hit the same wall.

Nothing left to dispatch here. Closed 2026-09-12 after a dispatched agent had to be redirected.

units.title: Per-output scaling: two densities, two sizes, one shell
units.note: REPLACES the old p1-039 unit, which landed on 2026-09-08 (apex-shell 690014a -> a90cef6, apex-os 678bb5d -> e67fab9). Left in place it would have offered finished work again: P1-039 and P1-041 are DONE, and resume.sh only calls a unit finished when EVERY item is done, so a unit carrying three hardware-blocked partials reads as READY forever. What is actually left here, and it is real dispatchable work: the shell resolves ONE scale factor through two singletons with 831 call sites across 82 files, so 'two outputs at compositor scale 1 with different densities each get their own size' was never attempted. The landed page states when the desk cannot share one size rather than claiming a per-output result it does not compute. Start at src/theme/scaling.js (the breakpoint table both the shell and node read) and src/theme/Metrics.qml, and treat the call-site count as the actual cost. The harness is already there: tests/run-scaling-test.sh brings up two headless outputs at different densities through tests/lib/headless.sh and is 30/0, so the assertion has somewhere to live on day one.

units.title: Integrate the firewall branches (work is finished, not merged)
units.note: DONE and pushed: task/p1-044-firewall-live 4cc3f4b (apex-os) and task/p1-044-firewall-settings e51412b (apex-shell). Optional follow-up its author names: apex firewall status --json so the shell page stops parsing prose. Two policy scope questions stay open on purpose -- LLMNR accepted on every interface, and mDNS accepting unicast from any source. Also open: katana's installed apex predates the firewall subcommand, and whether the page should stop offering commands that image cannot run is a judgement nobody has made. ALSO, from the P2-005 agent, measured with positive controls: a hotspot cannot work under the shipped policy, three independent ways -- forward is policy drop, the DHCP rule matches replies rather than a client's DISCOVER, and port 53 is shut. The exception mechanism itself is sound (631/445/2049 reopen immediately). And two lines in `apex devices network` state the current policy as fact and go stale the day it changes; ping task/p2-005-device-maturity when the policy moves.

units.note: REPLACES the old p1-050 unit, which was landed on apex-os roadmap/v2.2 as 1ab542c on 2026-09-07 (P1-050 done). Keeping p1-050 in the queue would have offered finished work again -- it read as HELD 'after p0-014' in the report, one dependency away from being dispatched twice. What is actually left, and it is a unit of its own: (1) no Cloudflare Worker or Durable Object relay is deployed -- the client exists in apex-remote-core, the server side does not; (2) no reconnect across network changes; (3) no mDNS discovery; (4) connection quality is not rendered; (5) apex-shell owes a QR pairing page and a paired-device page. P1-051 also stays partial for a reason NOT in this unit: --origin-policy remote stays refused until the device key lives in Android Keystore with setUserAuthenticationRequired, with a per-approval challenge and attestation -- that is p1-053a's work, and p0-014's CTAP2 verifier is the desktop half of it. Do not close P1-051 from here alone.

P1-051 and P1-052 stay partial and their remainders do NOT belong to this unit: P1-051 needs the key in Android Keystore with setUserAuthenticationRequired plus a per-approval challenge and attestation (that is p1-053a), and apex-shell owes it a QR page and a paired-device page. P1-052 needs a deployed Cloudflare Worker + Durable Object relay, reconnect across network changes, mDNS discovery and rendered connection quality -- a unit of its own. Do NOT re-dispatch p1-050; carve those two out instead.

All four hardening items the third integration round routed onward are on apex-os roadmap/v2.2 as ef87088..678bb5d (the broker's bare curl reading the owner's ~/.curlrc under root, 'reaches the same thing everywhere' made a declared fact, a bind test that bound nothing and passed, one curl in this build with a readable contract, and the MCP verbs documented in docs/agent-runtime.md).
